title: Chess in Telegram: understand skill, stakes and settlement
subtitle: A game result, a platform balance and a wallet withdrawal are different steps.
excerpt: Understand what makes Web3Chess a chess game, which activities are free, and how USDT match settlement differs from a wallet payout.
takeaways: Chess decisions determine the game; no result or income is guaranteed.
Free practice is separate from USDT player matches.
Match results credit a platform balance, with withdrawal handled separately.

content.text: A good reason to play chess is the game itself: a position to solve, an opponent to understand and a decision to improve. Adding an optional stake does not turn that decision into dependable income.
Web3Chess offers A.I. practice and an Academy. Use those activities to build familiarity with tactics, clocks and endgames. Practice does not promise money rewards.

Both players commit the same stake in a USDT player match. For a decided result, the combined pot is allocated between the winner, platform and referral pool. The current rules explain those allocations and the treatment of draws.

Deposits fund a platform balance held by Web3Chess. Match settlement credits that balance. A transfer to a personal wallet requires a separate withdrawal and its confirmation or review steps. The platform should not be described as non-custodial smart-contract escrow or instant on-chain settlement.
Choose the activity for your goal

items: To practise: play against A.I. without a stake.
To consider a player match: read the terms and current match rules first.

content.text: USDT player matches are 18+ and subject to local availability. You can lose your stake. Chess skill does not establish that a player will make a profit or replace a salary.
